mainTopic: Bringing a תודה on the festivals, and the timing of בל תאחר
overview: The amud opens by finishing the previous discussion: everyone agrees that נדרים and נדבות are not offered on יום טוב itself. The גמרא then quotes a ברייתא with three opinions about bringing a תודה on the festivals. The תנא קמא forbids it on פסח and on שבועות but allows it on סוכות, and the גמרא explains that this means חול המועד. It also explains that the line about פסח really refers to ערב פסח, because קדשים should not be put in a situation where they are more likely to become disqualified. רבי זירא challenges רבי שמעון's rule that all three festivals are alike. אביי answers that everyone allows bringing these offerings on חול המועד, and that the real argument is about when a person breaks בל תאחר: after any three רגלים, or only after three in order. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון allows a תודה even on יום טוב itself. He names סוכות because, unlike his father, he holds that סוכות itself is the deadline for vows. Finally, the תודה counts for שמחה but not for חגיגה, even if the person said so when he made the vow. The amud ends with a related question from ריש לקיש to רבי יוחנן that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Everyone agrees: no vowed or gift offerings on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: The previous discussion ends: all opinions agree that נדרים and נדבות are not offered on יום טוב itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: However, vow-offerings and gift-offerings: everyone agrees they are not offered on the festival day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up the previous discussion by naming the case on which there is no argument at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the disagreement was only about certain offerings connected to the festival. Here the גמרא limits that disagreement: personal offerings like נדרים and נדבות, which have nothing to do with the festival, are forbidden on יום טוב according to everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: Offerings a person obligates himself to bring ('I take upon myself an offering')
Offerings where a specific animal is set aside as a gift ('this animal is an offering')
Everyone agrees
The festival day itself, as opposed to חול המועד

phrases.english: However, vow-offerings and gift-offerings:

phrases.aramaic: דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל אֵין קְרֵיבִין בְּיוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.english: everyone agrees they are not offered on the festival day.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל נְדָרִים וּנְדָבוֹת דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל אֵין קְרֵיבִין בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the discussion from before this section by limiting the scope of the disagreement.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: נדרים and נדבות may not be offered on יום טוב according to all opinions.

steps.title: A parallel dispute: the first opinion on bringing a thanks-offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the same kind of disagreement appears in a ברייתא. The first opinion forbids a תודה on פסח and שבועות but allows it on סוכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: These תנאים are like those תנאים, as a ברייתא teaches: One may not bring a תודה on פסח because of the חמץ that comes with it, and not on שבועות because it is יום טוב. But a person may bring his תודה on סוכות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the argument it has been discussing also appears as a disagreement between תנאים in a ברייתא, and it begins quoting that ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תודה comes with forty loaves, ten of them חמץ, so it cannot be eaten on פסח. On שבועות the reason is different: it is יום טוב, and a personal offering is not brought then. סוכות is allowed, since it is a long festival that has days of חול המועד.

keyTerms.meaning: These תנאים are like those תנאים: the same disagreement appears elsewhere
Thanks-offering, brought together with forty loaves
Leavened bread; ten of the תודה loaves are חמץ
The name חז"ל use for שבועות

steps.confusionAlert: The two reasons are different. פסח is forbidden because of the חמץ loaves. שבועות is forbidden only because it is יום טוב.

phrases.english: And these tannaim are like those tannaim,
as it is taught: One may not bring a thanks-offering
on the festival of Matzot, because of the leavened bread that comes with it.
phrases.notes: Ten of the forty loaves that come with a תודה are חמץ.

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא בָּעֲצֶרֶת — מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא יוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.english: Nor on Shavuot, because it is a festival day.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מֵבִיא אָדָם תּוֹדָתוֹ בְּחַג הַסּוּכּוֹת.
phrases.english: But a person may bring his thanks-offering on the festival of Sukkot.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָנֵי תַּנָּאֵי כִּי הָנֵי תַּנָּאֵי דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Links the earlier disagreement to a parallel disagreement in a ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the תנא קמא, a תודה is not brought on פסח (because of חמץ) or on שבועות (because it is יום טוב), but it may be brought on סוכות.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: all three festivals follow the same rule
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון learns from a פסוק that whatever may be brought on פסח may be brought on שבועות and סוכות, and whatever may not be brought on פסח may not be brought on them either.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: The פסוק says 'on חג המצות, on חג השבועות, and on חג הסוכות.' Whatever comes on חג המצות comes on שבועות and סוכות, and whatever does not come on חג המצות does not come on שבועות and סוכות.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון disagrees with the first opinion and treats all three festivals as one unit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the פסוק lists the three festivals together, רבי שמעון compares them to each other. A תודה cannot come on פסח, so according to him it also cannot come on סוכות. That is the opposite of the תנא קמא, who allowed it on סוכות.

keyTerms.meaning: But the פסוק says: introduces a proof from a פסוק
The festival of שבועות
Whatever comes, meaning any offering that may be brought

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: הֲרֵי הוּא אוֹמֵר
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: But it says:
"On the festival of Matzot, on the festival of Shavuot, and on the festival of Sukkot,"
whatever comes on the festival of Matzot
comes on the festival of Shavuot and on the festival of Sukkot,
and whatever does not come on the festival of Matzot

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ בָּא בְּחַג הַשָּׁבוּעוֹת וּבְחַג הַסּוּכּוֹת.
phrases.english: does not come on the festival of Shavuot or on the festival of Sukkot.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר הֲרֵי הוּא אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the תנא קמא's permission to bring a תודה on סוכות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The three festivals are compared: an offering that is not brought on פסח, such as a תודה, is also not brought on שבועות or סוכות.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר son of רבי שמעון: a thanks-offering on סוכות counts for rejoicing
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון allows a תודה on סוכות. It fulfills the מצוה of שמחה, but not the obligation of חגיגה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says: A person may bring his תודה on סוכות, and he fulfills his obligation of שמחה with it, but he does not fulfill his obligation of חגיגה with it.
steps.whatsHappening: A third opinion in the ברייתא allows the תודה on סוכות and explains which festival obligation it can count for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מצוה of שמחה is fulfilled by eating the meat of שלמים-type offerings, so the meat of a תודה works for it. The חגיגה, however, is a specific festival offering, and a תודה cannot take its place.

keyTerms.meaning: His obligation
The מצוה to rejoice on the festival by eating offering meat
The special festival peace-offering every pilgrim must bring

steps.whatToRemember: There are three opinions in the ברייתא. The תנא קמא allows a תודה on סוכות. רבי שמעון seems to forbid it. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון allows it, and says it counts for שמחה but not for חגיגה. Later, אביי explains that the real argument is about בל תאחר (steps 12-14).

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon says:
A person may bring his thanks-offering on the festival of Sukkot,

phrases.aramaic: וְיוֹצֵא בָּהּ יְדֵי חוֹבָתוֹ מִשּׁוּם שִׂמְחָה,
phrases.english: and he fulfills his obligation of rejoicing with it,
but he does not fulfill with it the obligation of the festival offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר מֵבִיא אָדָם תּוֹדָתוֹ בְּחַג הַסּוּכּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third opinion: like the תנא קמא it allows the תודה on סוכות, and it also says which obligation the offering fulfills.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תודה brought on סוכות fulfills שמחה but not חגיגה.

steps.title: Isn't it obvious that there is no thanks-offering on פסח?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's first rule and asks why it needs to be said, since obviously חמץ cannot be brought on פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: 'One may not bring a תודה on חג המצות because of the חמץ in it.' That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא's first line and challenges it as stating something too obvious to need teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone knows חמץ is forbidden on פסח, so a ברייתא should not need to teach that a תודה, which has חמץ loaves, cannot be brought then. The question pushes the גמרא to find a new point hidden in this line.

keyTerms.meaning: That is obvious! Why does it need to be taught?

phrases.english: The Master said: One may not bring a thanks-offering
on the festival of Matzot, because of the leavened bread that comes with it.
That is obvious!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר אֵין מְבִיאִין תּוֹדָה בְּחַג הַמַּצּוֹת מִפְּנֵי חָמֵץ שֶׁבָּהּ פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to analyze the first line of the ברייתא quoted in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement that a תודה is not brought on פסח because of its חמץ.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule seems too obvious to need teaching, since חמץ is forbidden on פסח.

steps.title: It means ערב פסח: don't put sacrifices at risk of becoming disqualified
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is talking about the fourteenth of ניסן. A תודה is not brought then because that would cut short the time it may be eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בריה דרב יצחק said (some say it was רב שמואל בר אבא): Here we are dealing with the fourteenth of ניסן, and this תנא holds that one may not bring קדשים into a situation that leads to disqualification.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is not talking about פסח itself but about ערב פסח, and that it teaches a new rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תודה may normally be eaten for a day and a night. On ערב פסח, though, its חמץ loaves can only be eaten until midday. Bringing it then would leave food to be burned that could otherwise have been eaten, so the תנא forbids it.

keyTerms.meaning: Here we are dealing with: explains which case the source is really about
The fourteenth of ניסן, which is ערב פסח
A situation that causes disqualification

steps.whatToRemember: The rule against a תודה 'on פסח' really means ערב פסח. It is based on the principle אין מביאין קדשים לבית הפסול: don't bring קדשים into a situation that shortens the time they may be eaten.
steps.confusionAlert: On the fourteenth, חמץ is still allowed in the morning. The problem is not the חמץ itself but the shortened eating time.
steps.whyThisMatters: It introduces the general principle אין מביאין קדשים לבית הפסול, which the גמרא will keep discussing.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יִצְחָק,
phrases.english: Rav Adda son of Rav Yitzhak said,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר אַבָּא:
phrases.english: and some say it was Rav Shmuel bar Abba:
Here we are dealing with the fourteenth,
phrases.notes: He means the fourteenth of ניסן, the day before פסח.

phrases.aramaic: וְקָסָבַר: אֵין מְבִיאִין קָדָשִׁים לְבֵית הַפְּסוּל.
phrases.english: and he holds: one may not bring consecrated offerings into a situation of disqualification.
phrases.notes: Bringing it then shrinks the time to eat it, so more of it might end up disqualified and burned.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא בְּאַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר עָסְקִינַן וְקָסָבַר אֵין מְבִיאִין קָדָשִׁים לְבֵית הַפְּסוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5 by moving the case to ערב פסח.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-defining the case (אוקימתא) and identifying the principle behind the ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say only that a תודה can't be brought on פסח itself because of חמץ, which is obvious.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא means the fourteenth of ניסן and teaches that קדשים are not brought into a situation that shortens their eating time.

steps.title: Why no תודה on שבועות: no vow-offerings on a Festival
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says a תודה is not brought on עצרת because it is a יום טוב. The גמרא explains that this תנא holds נדרים ונדבות are not offered on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And not on שבועות, because it is a Festival day." The תנא holds that vow-offerings and gift-offerings may not be brought on a Festival day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the ברייתא and explains the reason behind it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תודה is a voluntary offering, so it belongs to the group of נדרים ונדבות. This תנא holds that such optional offerings may not be brought on יום טוב itself. That is why a תודה cannot be brought on שבועות, which is only one day of יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: Another name for שבועות
Vow-offerings and gift-offerings, which are voluntary קרבנות
"He holds": introduces the opinion that explains a ruling

phrases.english: And not on עצרת
phrases.notes: עצרת is the name the משנה and ברייתא use for שבועות.

phrases.english: because it is a Festival day.
He holds:

phrases.aramaic: נְדָרִים וּנְדָבוֹת אֵין קְרֵיבִין בְּיוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.english: Vow-offerings and gift-offerings are not offered on a Festival day.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָסָבַר: נְדָרִים וּנְדָבוֹת אֵין קְרֵיבִין בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining the first clause (פסח, step 6), the גמרא explains the second clause (שבועות).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first תנא holds נדרים ונדבות are not offered on יום טוב, so no תודה on שבועות.

steps.title: When on Sukkot may a תודה be brought?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא allows a תודה on סוכות. The גמרא asks when that means. It cannot mean יום טוב itself, because the ברייתא just said no תודה on שבועות since it is יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: "But a person may bring his תודה on the festival of סוכות." When? If you say on the יום טוב day itself, didn't you just say "not on שבועות because it is a Festival day"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the ברייתא and asks which days of סוכות it means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא already said a תודה is not brought on יום טוב. So the permission for סוכות cannot mean the יום טוב days of סוכות, or the ברייתא would contradict itself. The question pushes us toward the answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: "When?": asks about the exact time a rule applies
"If you say": brings up a possible reading so it can be rejected
"But didn't you say": points to an earlier statement that seems to clash

phrases.english: But a person may bring his thanks-offering
on the festival of סוכות.
When?
If you say on the Festival day itself
but didn't you say:

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא בָּעֲצֶרֶת מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא יוֹם טוֹב!
phrases.english: "And not on עצרת, because it is a Festival day"!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימַת? אִילֵּימָא בְּיוֹם טוֹב עַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the reason given in step 7 (no offerings on יום טוב) to ask what the סוכות permission means.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: On which days of סוכות may a תודה be brought, since it cannot be on יום טוב itself?

steps.title: It means on חול המועד
steps.stepSummary: The permission to bring a תודה on סוכות refers to חול המועד, the in-between days.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means on the intermediate days of the Festival.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the ברייתא is talking about חול המועד of סוכות, not the יום טוב days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This removes the contradiction. Optional offerings are not brought on יום טוב, but on חול המועד they may be. So the first תנא allows a תודה during חול המועד of סוכות.

keyTerms.meaning: The intermediate days of the Festival (חול המועד)
"Rather": brings the correct reading after rejecting the first one

steps.whatToRemember: According to the first תנא, no תודה is brought on יום טוב itself. On סוכות it may be brought only on חול המועד.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't wonder why the ברייתא allows חול המועד of סוכות but not of פסח. On פסח itself a תודה obviously can't be brought because of its חמץ loaves (step 5), and שבועות has no חול המועד at all.

phrases.english: Rather, on the intermediate days of the Festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא בְּחוּלּוֹ שֶׁל מוֹעֵד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא's permission for סוכות means חול המועד.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's rule quoted again
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי שמעון's rule again: whatever may come on חג המצות may come on שבועות and סוכות, and whatever may not, may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: The פסוק says "On the festival of מצות, on the festival of שבועות, and on the festival of סוכות." Whatever comes on חג המצות comes on שבועות and סוכות, and whatever does not come on חג המצות does not come on שבועות and סוכות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי שמעון's words again to set up a challenge. The next step will attack this rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since a תודה cannot be brought on פסח (because of חמץ), רבי שמעון's rule seems to say it cannot be brought on any festival, even on חול המועד of סוכות. That is exactly the point רבי זירא is about to question.

keyTerms.meaning: The festival of מצות, meaning פסח
"Behold it says": introduces a פסוק used as proof

phrases.english: רבי שמעון says:
Behold, it says
"On the festival of מצות, and on the festival of שבועות, and on the festival of סוכות"
whatever comes on the festival of מצות
comes on the festival of שבועות and on the festival of סוכות,
and whatever does not come on the festival of מצות

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ בָּא בְּחַג הַשָּׁבוּעוֹת וּבְחַג הַסּוּכּוֹת.
phrases.english: does not come on the festival of שבועות and on the festival of סוכות.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: הֲרֵי הוּא אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the first תנא's view, the גמרא returns to רבי שמעון's rule (first seen in step 3) as the target of a new challenge.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי שמעון: offerings that cannot come on פסח cannot come on שבועות or סוכות either.

steps.title: רבי זירא: We even chop wood on חול המועד, so surely offerings are allowed
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא objects: if we may even chop wood on חול המועד, surely נדרים ונדבות may be brought then. So how could רבי שמעון forbid them?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא objects: Now, if we even chop wood, is there any question about vow-offerings and gift-offerings?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא attacks the idea that רבי שמעון forbids a תודה on חול המועד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Chopping wood is real work, yet it is permitted on חול המועד for the needs of the Festival. If ordinary work like that is allowed, bringing a קרבן on חול המועד should certainly be allowed. So it seems strange that רבי שמעון's rule would forbid it.

keyTerms.meaning: "He strongly objects to it": introduces a sharp challenge
"We chop wood": cutting firewood, a kind of work
"Is it a question?": meaning this case should be even more obvious

phrases.english: רבי זירא objects to it:
Now, we even chop wood,
phrases.notes: He means chopping firewood on חול המועד, which is allowed even though it is real work.

phrases.english: is there any question about vow-offerings and gift-offerings?!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא: הַשְׁתָּא סַלּוֹתֵי מְסַלְּתִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the simple reading of רבי שמעון's rule quoted in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that רבי שמעון forbids נדרים ונדבות on חול המועד.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר-style argument: if real work like chopping wood is allowed on חול המועד, offering a קרבן should surely be allowed.

steps.title: אביי: Everyone allows offering; the argument is about בל תאחר
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that everyone agrees the offerings may be brought on חול המועד. The argument is about when a person becomes guilty of בל תאחר.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Everyone agrees that offering them is permitted. Where they argue is about when a person becomes liable for "you shall not delay."
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers רבי זירא by changing what the argument is about. רבי שמעון's rule is not about which days you may bring a קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bringing נדרים ונדבות on חול המועד is allowed according to everyone, so רבי זירא's question disappears. רבי שמעון's פסוק about the three festivals is used to count the time before a person is guilty of בל תאחר, the איסור of delaying a promised offering. The גמרא will explain the details of that counting next.

keyTerms.meaning: Offering, the actual bringing of the קרבן
"Everyone": all the opinions agree
The איסור against delaying a promised offering
"To be liable for it": the point when one becomes guilty

steps.whyThisMatters: This changes the whole argument in the ברייתא. It is no longer about the laws of the Festival, but about the timing of בל תאחר.

phrases.english: אביי said:
Regarding offering, everyone
does not argue that it is permitted.
Where they argue
is about becoming liable for "you shall not delay."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: בְּהַקְרָבָה כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דִּשְׁרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's challenge in step 11 by giving a new explanation of what the ברייתא argues about.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changes the subject of the argument: from permission to offer on the Festival to the timing of בל תאחר.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רבי שמעון forbids bringing a תודה on חול המועד of סוכות.
steps.terutzMaskana: Everyone allows offering on חול המועד. רבי שמעון's פסוק is about counting festivals for בל תאחר.

steps.title: The תנא קמא: three festivals in any order
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא holds that the Torah's 'three רגלים' for בל תאחר count even if they do not come in the order פסח, שבועות, סוכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first תנא holds: the Torah said 'three festivals,' even if they are not in their order.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues אביי's answer by explaining the first side of the argument about בל תאחר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the תנא קמא, any three רגלים in a row count, starting from whichever one comes first after the vow. So if סוכות is the first רגל after someone's vow, he should bring his תודה then. If he waits, he may not be able to bring it on פסח because of the חמץ loaves, or on שבועות, which has no חול המועד.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in a ברייתא or משנה
The three pilgrimage festivals: פסח, שבועות, סוכות
In their order, as the Torah lists them
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah

phrases.english: The first tanna holds:
The Merciful One said 'three festivals' —
phrases.notes: This is the count of three רגלים after which a person who has not yet brought his vowed offering breaks בל תאחר.

phrases.english: even not in their order.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנָּא קַמָּא סָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the first view in the בל תאחר argument that אביי just introduced.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Relocating the dispute to a different issue
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי זירא thought the argument was about whether offerings may be brought on חול המועד.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תנא קמא's view is about counting רגלים for בל תאחר: any three count, even out of order.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: the festivals must pass in order
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון holds that בל תאחר applies only when the three רגלים pass in the Torah's order.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון holds: in their order, yes; not in their order, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the other side of אביי's explanation, which is רבי שמעון's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי שמעון, the person breaks בל תאחר only after פסח, שבועות and סוכות have passed in that order. So someone who made a vow between פסח and שבועות can wait until סוכות of the next year. That is why רבי שמעון does not need to tell him to rush and bring the offering on this year's סוכות.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes
No

steps.whatToRemember: The argument is not about whether offerings may be brought on חול המועד. Everyone allows that. The argument is about when בל תאחר starts: any three רגלים (תנא קמא), or three רגלים in order (רבי שמעון).

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon holds:
In their order, yes,
phrases.notes: Yes, he breaks בל תאחר once the three festivals have passed.

phrases.english: not in their order, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to the תנא קמא in the same explanation.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Relocating the dispute to a different issue
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed רבי שמעון forbade נדרים ונדבות on חול המועד.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון only means that the three רגלים must pass in order before בל תאחר applies.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר son of רבי שמעון: a thanks-offering on סוכות
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא quotes רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון: a person may bring his תודה on סוכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says: a person may bring his תודה on the festival of סוכות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the next opinion in the ברייתא so it can examine what it means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the surface, this sounds just like the תנא קמא, who also allowed a תודה on סוכות. The גמרא will now ask what new point רבי אלעזר is adding.

keyTerms.meaning: Thanks-offering, brought together with loaves, some of them חמץ
The festival of סוכות

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon says:
A person may bring his thanks-offering on the festival of Sukkot.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next opinion in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תודה may be brought on סוכות.

steps.title: When does he mean? Not חול המועד
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks when on סוכות he means. It rules out חול המועד, because then he would just be repeating the תנא קמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: When? If you say on חול המועד, that is the same as the תנא קמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which part of סוכות רבי אלעזר is talking about, and rejects the first possible answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא already allowed a תודה on חול המועד of סוכות (step 9). If רבי אלעזר meant the same thing, he would have nothing new to say. So he must mean something else.

keyTerms.meaning: When?
If you say
That is the same as
The in-between days of the festival

phrases.english: When?
If you say on the intermediate days of the festival —
that is the same as the first tanna.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימַת? אִילֵּימָא בְּחוּלּוֹ שֶׁל מוֹעֵד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the meaning of the statement just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי אלעזר means חול המועד or the יום טוב itself.

steps.title: He means יום טוב itself
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר means the יום טוב day itself, because he holds that נדרים ונדבות may be offered on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he means on יום טוב, and he holds that נדרים ונדבות are offered on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי אלעזר is talking about the יום טוב day itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows that רבי אלעזר disagrees with the opinion that bans נדרים ונדבות on יום טוב. In his view, even a תודה, which is a נדר or נדבה, may be brought on the festival day.

keyTerms.meaning: Vowed offerings and freewill offerings
Are offered
And he holds

phrases.english: Rather, on the festival day itself,
and he holds that vow-offerings and gift-offerings
may be offered on a festival day.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He means יום טוב itself, and he holds נדרים ונדבות may be brought on יום טוב.

steps.title: Why mention סוכות specifically?
steps.stepSummary: If he allows נדרים ונדבות on any יום טוב, why does he single out סוכות?
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is different about סוכות that he mentioned it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question about why רבי אלעזר chose סוכות as his example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he allows these offerings on every יום טוב, he could have said 'a person may bring his תודה on יום טוב.' Naming סוכות suggests there is something special about it.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different?
That he mentioned it

phrases.english: And what is different about the festival of Sukkot
that he mentioned it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי שְׁנָא חַג הַסּוּכּוֹת דְּנָקֵט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the answer of step 17 and asks about the wording.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why סוכות is singled out if every יום טוב is allowed.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר follows his own view on בל תאחר
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר is following his own view. A ברייתא records a disagreement over why the פסוק names חג הסוכות. רבי שמעון says it teaches that סוכות must be the last of the three רגלים for בל תאחר. רבי אלעזר's own reading follows in the next step.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון follows his own reasoning, as a ברייתא teaches: רבי שמעון says, the פסוק did not need to say 'חג הסוכות,' since it was already talking about it. Why was it said? To teach that this one is last.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי אלעזר names סוכות because of his own view on בל תאחר. It first quotes his father רבי שמעון's reading of the פסוק, which רבי אלעזר will argue with in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra words 'חג הסוכות' get two readings. רבי שמעון says they teach that the three רגלים must end with סוכות (this is his view from step 14). רבי אלעזר disagrees and reads them differently in the next step, and his reading is what explains why he singles out סוכות.

keyTerms.meaning: Following his own reasoning
It did not need to be said
Last

steps.whatToRemember: Father and son disagree. For רבי שמעון, סוכות must be the last of the three רגלים. For רבי אלעזר, סוכות itself is the deadline (step 20).
steps.whyThisMatters: This ties רבי אלעזר's practical advice about a תודה to his own rule on how בל תאחר works, which differs from his father's.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon follows his own reasoning,
as it is taught: Rabbi Shimon says:
It did not need to say 'the festival of Sukkot,'
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק listing the three festivals, דברים 16:16.

phrases.english: since the verse was speaking about it.
Why was it said?
To say that this one is last.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לְטַעְמֵיהּ, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 18 by quoting the ברייתא in which רבי שמעון and רבי אלעזר disagree. The answer is completed in step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: סוכות is singled out because of רבי אלעזר's own view that סוכות itself is what makes a person late (step 20), unlike רבי שמעון, who says it must be the last of three.

steps.title: סוכות itself is what makes a person late
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון reads the פסוק as saying that סוכות itself is the deadline for בל תאחר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר son of רבי שמעון says: the פסוק comes to teach that this festival, סוכות, is what causes a person to be late.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's own reading of the פסוק. This explains why he singled out סוכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For him, בל תאחר is not about counting three festivals. It means a person must bring all his promised offerings by סוכות, the last festival of the year. That is why bringing a תודה on סוכות itself matters so much to him.

keyTerms.meaning: causes; here, sets the deadline that makes someone late
the prohibition against delaying a promised offering

steps.whyThisMatters: It closes the question from Step 18. סוכות is singled out because it is the deadline for every vow from that year.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon says:
It comes to say that this one causes [the lateness].
phrases.notes: "This one" means סוכות itself, which sets the deadline.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: לוֹמַר שֶׁזֶּה גּוֹרֵם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי אלעזר's own reading of the פסוק, completing the answer begun in Step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: סוכות itself is the deadline for בל תאחר, no matter how many festivals have gone by.

steps.title: The תודה counts for שמחה but not for חגיגה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: a תודה brought on the חג fulfills the שמחה obligation but not the חגיגה obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: With this תודה he fulfills his obligation of rejoicing, but he does not fulfill his obligation of the festival offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the ברייתא and quotes its next ruling about what a תודה counts for on the חג.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two festival duties. One is שמחה, which means eating meat from שלמים. The other is חגיגה, a set offering everyone must bring. The ברייתא says the תודה works for the first but not the second.

keyTerms.meaning: the festival duty to rejoice by eating offering meat
the required festival שלמים offering
fulfills an obligation

phrases.english: And he fulfills with it [the obligation] of rejoicing,
phrases.notes: "It" is the תודה he brought on the חג.

phrases.english: but he does not fulfill with it [the obligation] of the festival offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְיוֹצֵא בָּהּ מִשּׁוּם שִׂמְחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ברייתא from Step 15 and quotes its next clause.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תודה brought on the חג counts for שמחה but not for חגיגה.

steps.title: Why say it? An obligation must come from חולין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא needs to say this. A required offering can only come from an animal that is not already holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: That's obvious! The חגיגה is something you are required to bring, and anything required must come only from non-holy animals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא for saying something that seems too obvious to need saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known rule that a required offering can't be brought from an animal already made holy for something else. The תודה was already holy as a תודה, so of course it can't also count as the חגיגה. So why did the ברייתא bother saying it?

keyTerms.meaning: it's obvious
something a person is required to bring
non-holy property, not yet set aside for the מקדש

phrases.english: That's obvious! It is an obligatory matter,
and anything that is obligatory
comes only from non-holy property!

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling in Step 21 as too obvious to need saying.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's line that a תודה does not count for חגיגה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A known rule already teaches that a required offering must come from חולין, so this line seems pointless.

steps.title: Even if he said so at the start
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is needed for a case where the person stated at the start that the תודה should also count as his חגיגה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed for a case where he spelled it out at the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ruling teaches something new: it holds even when the person said at the start that the תודה should also count for חגיגה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think that setting this condition when making the vow would let one animal count for both. The ברייתא teaches that even then, it does not count as the חגיגה.

keyTerms.meaning: it is only needed for (a special case)
he spelled it out; he stated it clearly

phrases.english: No, it is needed
[to teach] that even though he spelled it out.
phrases.notes: He said at the time of his vow that the תודה should also count as his חגיגה.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא, דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּפָרֵישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 22 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case to a new situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Saying at the start that the תודה should also count for חגיגה might make it work.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even with that stated condition, the תודה does not count as the חגיגה.

steps.title: ריש לקיש's similar question to רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא connects this to a question ריש לקיש asked רבי יוחנן about someone who vows a תודה and says he will use it for חגיגה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like what ריש לקיש asked רבי יוחנן: if someone says, 'I take upon myself a תודה, and I will use it for my חגיגה,' or says, 'I am a נזיר...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a parallel question that ריש לקיש asked רבי יוחנן. It is setting up a discussion that continues on the next daf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש asks about exactly the case from Step 23: a vow that tries to make a תודה count for חגיגה too. He also starts a second case about a נזיר. The full question and answer come next.

keyTerms.meaning: asked him
I take upon myself; the wording of a vow
a person who vows to avoid wine, haircuts and טומאת מת

phrases.aramaic: כְּדִבְעָא מִנֵּיהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ
phrases.english: As Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish asked
of Rabbi Yochanan:
One who says, 'It is upon me to bring a thanks offering,'
'and I will fulfill with it my festival offering,'
[or:] 'I am a nazirite'
phrases.notes: The question breaks off here and continues on the next daf.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּדִבְעָא מִנֵּיהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ מֵרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Links the case from Step 23 to a known question asked between אמוראים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a vow that sets aside a תודה and also says it will count for חגיגה work, and how does a similar נזיר case work?
